selected_specification: Original v2.0 12-factor phase-specific model (6 batting sub-formulas; 6 bowling sub-formulas; bounded [0; 100])
decision_rationale: Audited baseline is mathematically stable; continuous; bounded; and validated across 188330 deliveries
decision_nature: Methodological decision supported by audit evidence
limitations_and_uncertainties: PI sub-weights derived from expert calibration rather than automated statistical optimization

selected_specification: Original v2.0 spell-based workload: W_spell = min(100; (balls_in_spell_before / 12) * 100)
alternatives_investigated: Experimental cumulative innings workload: W_innings = min(100; (balls_in_innings_before / 24) * 100)
decision_rationale: Cumulative formula introduces severe phase-confounding (r > 0.85 with match overs); deflates PP pressure by -2.84 pts; inflates Death PI by +6.77 pts; collapses bowling ranking correlation to r=0.7884; and disqualifies 15 Tier 1 bowlers
decision_nature: Methodological decision supported by empirical audit evidence
limitations_and_uncertainties: Spell-based formula resets workload when bowler rests 2+ overs; which remains an architectural limitation to be addressed via exponential decay in future versions (v3.0)

selected_specification: BRS3 three-component formula: 0.45 * Score_SR + 0.35 * Score_Surv + 0.20 * Score_Diff
alternatives_investigated: Official v2.0 four-component formula (with Boundary Execution); Equal-weighted formula; Survival-heavy formula
decision_rationale: Strike Rate and Boundary Execution are highly collinear (r = 0.963; VIF > 14); removing boundary execution eliminates double-counting while preserving scoring acceleration and wicket preservation
decision_nature: Methodological simplification supported by collinearity audit
limitations_and_uncertainties: BRS3 does not prove boundary execution has zero independent information; nor is it proven to be objectively superior across all game contexts

selected_specification: Original v2.0 four-component formula: 0.40 * Score_Econ + 0.25 * Score_Wk + 0.20 * Score_Dot + 0.15 * Score_Diff
alternatives_investigated: Experimental containment-weighted formula (incorporating boundary suppression and heavy dot weighting)
decision_rationale: Containment formula introduced severe multicollinearity with economy (r > 0.90) and diluted wicket value without improving stability; original BoRS balances run prevention (40%); wicket-taking (25%); pressure control (20%); and clutch differential (15%)
decision_nature: Methodological decision supported by audit evidence
limitations_and_uncertainties: Weights are calibrated rather than empirically optimized; clutch differential has higher variance for low-sample bowlers

selected_specification: Constant global shrinkage parameter K = 50.0 legal deliveries across all components
alternatives_investigated: Variable K (K=30; K=75); Empirical Bayes hierarchical priors; Unregularized observed rates
decision_rationale: K=50 (approx 8.2 overs) smoothly shrinks small-sample noise toward global population means without over-penalizing moderate-sample players; verified stable in Step 14.1 (rho = 0.9984-0.9989)
decision_nature: Practical policy choice calibrated to T20 format
limitations_and_uncertainties: K=50 is a reasonable heuristic format-calibrated parameter rather than a statistically proven unique optimum

selected_specification: Rule B dual-threshold: Tier 1 requires N >= 60 OR (N >= 50 AND M >= 6); Tier 2 requires N >= 40 (not in T1); Excluded N < 40
alternatives_investigated: Official v2.0 single threshold (N >= 60); Rule A (N >= 75); Rule C (Phase-specific thresholds)
decision_rationale: Protects sample depth while accommodating multi-match clutch performers who accumulated 50-59 balls across 6+ matches; prevents single-match high-ball concentration distortions
limitations_and_uncertainties: Threshold numbers (60; 50; 6; 40) are pragmatic governance boundaries rather than statistically derived transition cutoffs

selected_specification: Strictly PI > 60.0 (High Pressure) vs PI <= 60.0 (Low / Moderate Pressure)
alternatives_investigated: Boundary-inclusive PI >= 60.0; Three-tier splits; Dynamic percentile thresholds
decision_rationale: Established operational standard maintained throughout Steps 4-14; exactly 38 baseline and 31 experimental deliveries sit at PI == 60.0 and belong to moderate pressure
limitations_and_uncertainties: Boundary is a sharp binary cutoff on a continuous [0; 100] scale; balls at 59.9 and 60.1 receive discrete classification

selected_specification: Full population evaluation (816 batters; 589 bowlers); followed by Tier 1 filtering and Top 10 selection
alternatives_investigated: Pre-filtered elite candidate pool; Optimizing weights solely to fit expected Top 10 roster
decision_rationale: Full population evaluation prevents truncation selection bias and ensures valid empirical population priors
limitations_and_uncertainties: Tail rankings among low-sample unregularized players have high variance; mitigated by Tier filtering

selected_specification: Retrospective measurement and ranking of observed historical player reliability under pressure (2022-2026)
alternatives_investigated: Predictive forecasting; Machine learning win-probability models; Future performance prediction
decision_rationale: The model's verified mathematical objective is retrospective performance measurement; not predictive forecasting
limitations_and_uncertainties: Historical reliability under pressure does not guarantee future performance in different conditions; teams; or roles

component: Player Role Classification & Dual Eligibility Policy
selected_specification: All eligible players who bat or bowl under pressure are evaluated; all-rounders are intentionally eligible for both batting and bowling rankings based purely on performance and Rule B qualification
alternatives_investigated: Restricting batting rankings to specialist top-order batters; excluding bowling all-rounders; single-role designation
decision_rationale: The system ranks performance reliability under pressure, not nominal squad labels; finishers and lower-order power-hitters face heavy death-over pressure and deserve ranking on merit; removing qualified players like Jamie Overton introduces subjective selection bias
limitations_and_uncertainties: Selectors must distinguish pure reliability ranking under pressure from positional roster construction when picking a balanced XI
